subject: English
passage: "A Distant Mirror," a book by American historian Barbara Tuchman, chronicles the details of medieval daily life, while her work "The Guns of August" examines the weighty origins of World War I. Regardless of the time period she studies, Tuchman questions conventional historical interpretations. ______ she challenges her own assumptions, no matter the era.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Choice A is the best answer because 'Indeed' provides emphatic reinforcement of the previous claim. The text establishes that Tuchman 'questions conventional historical interpretations' regardless of time period, and the sentence following the blank restates this same characterization: 'she challenges her own assumptions, no matter the era.' These statements express the same idea using synonymous language. 'Indeed' signals that what follows will confirm and strengthen the point just made, which is precisely the logical relationship between these two sentences describing Tuchman's consistent intellectual approach.
